faqs.q: What even is ACM-VIT?
faqs.a: We're the VIT Vellore student chapter of ACM - the Association for Computing Machinery, the world's largest computing society. Founded in 2009, we're the campus's excuse to build things, break things, and occasionally fix them before a deadline.

faqs.q: What's the difference between ACM and ACM-VIT?
faqs.a: ACM is the global parent organisation - research journals, the Turing Award, very serious people in blazers. ACM-VIT is the local chapter that turns all that prestige into hackathons, workshops, and a group chat that never sleeps.

faqs.q: Do I need to already know how to code?
faqs.a: No. Bring curiosity, we'll supply the Stack Overflow tabs. Plenty of our best builders walked in not knowing what a for-loop was and walked out shipping projects.

faqs.q: Is ACM-VIT only for Computer Science students?
faqs.a: Not even close. We have Design, Management and Research folks who've never opened a terminal in their life. If you can bring a skill, we can find a use for it.

faqs.q: Do I have to be a VIT Vellore student?
faqs.a: To be a chapter member, yes - we're the VIT Vellore chapter, and the work happens on campus. Our events are a different story: plenty are open campus-wide, and a few go well beyond VIT.

faqs.q: How do I join ACM-VIT?
faqs.a: We run one recruitment cycle a year - a form, a couple of rounds, mild nerves. Keep an eye on our Instagram or drop a note through our contact form and we'll point you to the open cycle.

faqs.q: What is ACM-W, and how do I join it?
faqs.a: ACM-W is our sister chapter, started by ACM-VIT to back women in STEM and registered as a chapter under ACM International in its own right. There's no separate application: join ACM-VIT and you're in, because the same members run both chapters.

faqs.q: Is there a membership fee?
faqs.a: Nope. Your only real cost is time, sleep, and possibly a bit of your GPA during exam season.

faqs.q: Does joining make me a member of ACM International?
faqs.a: Not automatically. We're an officially recognised ACM student chapter, but individual ACM International membership is a separate paid signup on acm.org, with the Digital Library and global perks attached. Chapter membership gets you the people and the projects; the acm.org card is yours to pick up if you want it.

faqs.q: I'm a first-year - can I still apply?
faqs.a: First years are exactly who we're looking for. Most of our current leads started as clueless freshers who happened to show up on time once.

faqs.q: Recruitment is closed. Can I still get involved?
faqs.a: Yes. Attend our open events and workshops, contribute to our projects on GitHub, or just show up to what's public. Doors reopen once a year - you won't miss the next cycle if you're already around.

faqs.q: What are ACM-VIT's domains?
faqs.a: Five of them: Technical, Competitive Coding, Design, Management, and Research. Each runs its own projects and events - you can browse what they're building right now.

faqs.q: Can I be part of multiple domains?
faqs.a: You pick one core domain at recruitment, but cross-domain collaboration happens constantly in practice - most of our better projects are the result of two domains arguing productively.

faqs.q: What does the Design domain actually do?
faqs.a: Everything you're looking at right now, including these cassette illustrations - plus posters, brand systems, and the occasional 3am Figma disagreement.

faqs.q: What kind of events does ACM-VIT run?
faqs.a: Hackathons, technical workshops, speaker sessions, CTFs, and community programs like Hour of Code and Kickstart Learn. There's usually something on the calendar.

faqs.q: Are events open to non-members?
faqs.a: Most of them, yes. Some are exclusive to registered members, some are open campus-wide, and a few go beyond VIT entirely. Registration details go out on our socials closer to the date.

faqs.q: How do I find out what's coming up?
faqs.a: Our calendar page has the full schedule - or follow us on Instagram, which you're probably already refreshing anyway.

faqs.q: Can I contribute to ACM-VIT projects without being a member?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Most of what we build lives on GitHub and takes pull requests happily. Have a look at what we're currently shipping.

faqs.q: What's z0d1ak?
faqs.a: Our competitive Capture The Flag team, currently ranked among the best in the country. If "capture the flag" makes you think of a camping trip, this is not that.

faqs.q: Does ACM-VIT actually ship real software, or is this all workshops?
faqs.a: Both. We've contributed to SGLang's documentation, won hackathons on- and off-campus, and shipped more side projects than fit on one page. The receipts are all there.

faqs.q: What's Forktober?
faqs.a: Our open source month. A pile of ACM-VIT repositories, issues sized for first-time contributors, and maintainers who actually read your pull request. Membership not required - anyone can pick up an issue.

faqs.q: What's GREP?
faqs.a: Our bi-annual technical newsletter. Yes, named after the command - we thought it was clever too, and we stand by it.

faqs.q: Is there merch?
faqs.a: There is, but it's a members-only wardrobe. Join the chapter and it's yours to earn; until then, you just get to admire ours.

faqs.q: Can I write for the blog?
faqs.a: Members write most of it, on whatever they've been nerding out about that month. If you're outside the chapter and have something worth reading, pitch it through our contact form.

faqs.q: Something went wrong at an event. Who do I tell?
faqs.a: Tell us. We have a code of conduct and it isn't decoration - reports go through the contact form and reach the board directly, and we'd rather hear about it late than never.

faqs.q: Who do I talk to about partnerships or sponsorships?
faqs.a: Send a message through our contact form and we'll get back to you - usually faster than your professor replies to email.

faqs.q: Why is everything on this site designed like a cassette tape?
faqs.a: Because the web has enough stock photos of laptops. We'd rather it had more analog nostalgia and reels that actually spin.
